clue.text: See 5
Struggle against work model

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone resists the job of modelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight against something is to resist it, which this verb means.

clue.text: Mummy, mummy, naughty naughty!

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the famous Egyptian mummy
again the boy pharaoh, Tut, the best-known mummy

explanation.surface: A child scolds: 'Mummy, mummy, that's naughty!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' is not a mother but Tutankhamun, the Egyptian mummy known as King Tut.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild disapproval, a click of the tongue said to tell someone off.

clue.text: Amid 17, shorten form of an organ

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the shortened word goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer to 17 down means a frenzy, which is panic

indicators.note: shorten means cut the word short by its final letter

parts.note: to form something is to create it

explanation.surface: Amid hysteria, someone shortens the form of an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the answer at 17 down, whose synonym is needed, not the word itself; 'form' is a verb here, and 'shorten' trims its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the gland behind the stomach that makes insulin, so it means relating to an organ.

clue.text: Time to plug utter rogue, primarily, as lustful type

indicators.note: plugging a gap means filling it, so the time letter goes inside the word for utter

parts.note: to utter is to say

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of rogue counts

explanation.surface: It is time to stop up an utter rogue, a lecherous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to plug' puts T inside SAY; 'primarily' takes R from rogue. 'utter' looks like an adjective but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth this goat-like woodland creature was known for lechery, hence any lecherous man.

clue.text: Unlikely World Cup celebrity chose to put balls past me

indicators.note: past means beyond or after, so the shuffled letters come after the setter's name

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle writes as Paul, so 'me' gives his pen name

indicators.note: as in a balls-up, a mess, so the letters of the phrase beside it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A football star chose to put balls past me, the goalkeeper, at the World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' shuffles CHOSE TO PUT into THE OCTOPUS; 'past' puts it after PAUL, which is the setter speaking as 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: This cephalopod at a German aquarium became famous for apparently predicting the results of matches at the 2010 tournament.

clue.text: Fabrication of leader in Observer that's top copy

indicators.note: fabrication is making something up, so the letters are built into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper's top story is said to be a fabrication by its lead writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader in' picks O from Observer, a British Sunday newspaper; 'Fabrication of' rearranges O with THATS TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name for a photographic duplicate of a document, so it is a kind of copy.

clue.text: Druggie's democratic or republican monarch?

parts.note: the two main American parties, so US for United States
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Asks whether a drug addict is a democratic or a republican monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes illegal drugs is commonly called by this word.

clue.text: Test carrying university over to class

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the test word holds the others

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

explanation.surface: A test involves the university going over to a class.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means placed above, so the university letter comes before the little word; 'carrying' wraps the test around both.
explanation.definitionFit: A small teaching session with a tutor is a kind of class.

clue.text: English gun ships showing flags

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, an arm
arks are ships, like Noah's

explanation.surface: English gunships are flying flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag something is to mark it out for attention or a purpose, which this verb means.

clue.text: G8 leader installed

definitions.meaning: the Russian politician, a leader at the G8 summits
set in place, like a new kitchen fitted

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Russian leader doubles as the two-word phrase meaning fitted or set in position.

clue.text: Sofa, perhaps, where Torode's first broadcast rejected by diner

indicators.note: the first letter of the chef's name is wanted, not the whole name
something rejected is sent back, so the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering it widely
a diner is someone who eats, an eater

explanation.surface: A chef's first television show is turned down by a restaurant customer.
explanation.walkthrough: John Torode is a TV chef (MasterChef), which gives the cooking picture. 'rejected' turns SOW into WOS; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa built for two people is one example of a seat for a pair, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Dinosaur and ferret — one's one's one

definitions.note: read as 'one is the [answer] of one', a mathematical fact about the number one

parts.note: an old-fashioned, conventional person, a fuddy-duddy
to ferret is to rummage or search about

explanation.surface: A dinosaur and a ferret are listed, followed by a stuttering string of ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a puzzle in itself: one multiplied by itself is one, so one's square root is one; the answer slots in as the middle 'one's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, the number which multiplied by itself gives one is one itself, which the odd phrase spells out.

clue.text: Huge beast knocks shopping centre off island

indicators.note: with 'off', to knock something off is to remove it from the rest
with 'knocks', the shopping-centre word is taken away from the island's name

parts.note: the Spanish Balearic island, also spelt Majorca
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Someone demolishes a shopping centre on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks ... off' removes MALL from MALLORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a very large marine mammal, so a huge beast describes it well.

clue.text: Shake up orange vigorously, carried by rocket

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the jumbled fruit goes within the other word

parts.note: to rocket is to rise quickly

indicators.note: something done vigorously is shaken hard, so the letters of the fruit are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shakes up an orange hard before it is carried by a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orange' is the fruit's letters, not a colour; 'vigorously' jumbles them and 'carried by' places them within the word for rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake up an organisation is to restructure it, to arrange it differently.

clue.text: Acknowledgment, the result of lying face down behind cow?

definitions.meaning: a gesture of praise or congratulation for a job well done

definitions.text: the result of lying face down behind cow?
definitions.meaning: lying prone behind a cow, you might end up with dung landing on your back

explanation.definitionFit: A gesture of congratulation is a light touch on someone's back, and a cowpat could land there literally.

clue.text: Wine lover taking gallons from pigeonhole, sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so the remaining letters stagger into a new order
with 'from', taking something from a word removes it
with 'taking', the gallons letter is removed from the long word

explanation.surface: A wine lover, drunk, takes gallons from a pigeonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' drops G from PIGEONHOLE, leaving PIEONHOLE; 'sloshed' rearranges it. 'sloshed' fits the wine picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This rather formal word, from Greek for wine and loving, means a connoisseur or enthusiast of wine.

clue.text: Vessel placed in middle of maidservant's drawer

indicators.note: placed in means set inside, so the boat goes inside the letters
only some central letters of the long word are taken

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A ship is placed in the middle of a maidservant's chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like part of a chest, but it means someone who draws; the 's is a link-free possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who draws is a drawer, and one making quick rough drawings is this.

clue.text: Sound of snake crying more, in a frenzy

indicators.note: sound of signals the words are heard, so hiss and tearier are said together

parts.note: a snake's noise is a hiss, and crying more is tearier

explanation.surface: The noise of a snake weeping more, in a wild frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' says 'hiss tearier' aloud; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of uncontrolled emotion or wild excitement is this, so it is a frenzy.

clue.text: Block of flats, perhaps?

parts.note: in music a flat is a symbol lowering a note, and a cluster of them at the start of a stave sets the tonality

explanation.definitionFit: The group of sharps or flats at the start of a stave of written music is the musical notation for tonality.

clue.text: Natural growth's cut twice, creating muscle

indicators.note: the mushroom cuts into the word for twice, sitting inside it

parts.note: bis is Latin and French for twice, the call for an encore
a cep is a wild mushroom, a natural growth; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A natural growth is cut twice, making muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is the call French audiences use for an encore. 'growth' suggests a tumour, but it is a mushroom, and 'cut' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm is named for its two heads.

clue.text: Unconscious state, way high otherwise

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
up means high
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'

explanation.surface: Being very high, or something else, leaves one in an unconscious state.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed state of near-unconsciousness, often from drink or drugs, is this.

clue.text: Wizard of Oz companion, little one close to Dorothy's heart?

indicators.note: beside, so the next letter sits right next to the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre letter

explanation.surface: A small child is dear to the heart of the girl in a famous film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' picks O, the middle letter of DOROTHY; 'close to' sets it beside TOT. Toto is Dorothy's dog, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the story the small dog travels everywhere with Dorothy, making him her constant companion.

clue.text: Buff model is plastic, injecting last of polypropylene

indicators.note: injected material goes inside, so the end letter is put into the reshaped letters
to model clay is to shape it, so the letters beside it are reshaped
only the final letter of the long word is wanted

explanation.surface: A model is made of plastic with polypropylene injected into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges IS PLASTIC into SPCIALIST; 'injecting' puts E, the final letter from 'last of polypropylene', after SP. 'model' looks like a noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge, so the word means an expert in a field.

clue.text: Family planning's ultimate ring

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A family plans its final wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' takes G, the last letter of planning. 'ring' is a sound here, not jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic ringing noise, as of a bell or struck metal, is this.

clue.text: Modern composer's rules of grammar: double negatives are a ___ ?

definitions.text: rules of grammar: double negatives are a ___ ?
definitions.meaning: the blank wants a word for something forbidden, itself a doubled negative word

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer's surname also means a thing not allowed, written as two negatives side by side.

clue.text: Girl on musical instrument, not piano — another one?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
not signals that the piano letter is left out of the instrument

parts.note: the harp is a stringed musical instrument
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl sits at a musical instrument without a piano, asking for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to 'musical instrument': the answer is a second instrument. 'on' places the girl after the shortened harp.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ is a further musical instrument, so 'another one' refers back to the instrument named in the clue.

clue.text: I'm a drinker, say, to become hard and cold

indicators.note: say signals the words are heard rather than read, so it is their sound that counts

parts.note: a drinker could say 'I sup', sup meaning to drink in sips

explanation.surface: A drinker declares himself, perhaps, about to turn hard and cold.
explanation.definitionFit: When water on a surface freezes it grows solid and chilly, which is what this phrasal verb describes.

clue.text: Mixture of okra and wee, stirred again

indicators.note: a mixture blends things, so the letters of the vegetable and the word wee are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mixture of okra and something unpleasant is stirred again in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture of' rearranges OKRA and WEE together; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stirred from sleep a second time is to have come round again, the past tense of a verb of waking.

clue.text: Feminist dressing as long-haired biker?

indicators.note: dressing means wrapping round like a garment, so the feminist's name surrounds the little word

parts.note: Germaine Greer is a famous feminist writer

explanation.surface: A feminist dresses up as a hairy motorcyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocker or biker of the 1950s and 60s with long greased-back hair was called by this slang word.
